yesNoText: Yes, with care. The Knight of Cups is a positive card of offers, romance and invitations, so it generally leans yes. Check substance against charm. Reversed, the answer shifts to no or maybe: the offer may be insincere, unreliable or built more on feeling than on facts.
melissaLine: Enjoy the romance, but judge him on what he does on an ordinary Tuesday, not on how beautifully he talks.

name: Queen of Cups
metaDescription: Queen of Cups tarot card meaning: upright, reversed, love and yes or no. Intuition, compassion and keeping your own cup full.
intro: The Queen of Cups sits on a carved throne at the edge of the sea, with the waves washing at her feet. She holds an ornate, closed chalice topped with a cross and decorated with angels, and gazes at it intently. She is intuition and compassion, and she keeps her depth to herself until she trusts you.
upright:
She is the friend who knows what is wrong from the way you said hello. The Queen of Cups is emotionally mature, compassionate and intuitive. She listens without rushing to fix, and her feelings are deep but not chaotic. The cup is closed, which means she does not pour herself into everyone. She chooses who gets the inside.

This card invites you to trust your gut reading of a room and a person. You noticed when the tone changed in the meeting, or the way he did not look up from his phone. You were probably right. It also reminds you to look after your own cup: empathy is a resource, not an infinite supply. Say no to the friend who only calls when she is in crisis. Caring deeply does not mean being available around the clock. Be kind, and be selective.
reversed:
Reversed, the Queen is overwhelmed, or her feelings are bent out of shape. She may soak up everyone else's mood until she cannot tell hers apart, cry at the supermarket and not know why, or use her sensitivity as a weapon: sulking, guilt-tripping, martyrdom. Intuition can become paranoia when you are exhausted.

Protect your boundaries. Switch off notifications, stop being the group therapist and find your own support. When you read something into a silence, check it with a question rather than a theory. Compassion needs a floor, and yours is currently soaking wet.
love: Single, you may be drawn to emotionally deep, kind people, and you offer the same. Be careful not to mother a man who needs fixing. In a relationship, she is a card of tenderness and attunement, with a need for emotional safety. Tell your partner what you need, as you cannot expect him to guess. With an ex or situationship, your feelings may be strong and your boundaries weaker. Compassion for them can continue, without letting them back in. Keep the cup closed until trust is earned.
career: Your intuition and empathy are professional skills now: reading clients, calming tense teams, spotting who is upset in the meeting. Suited to caring, creative and counselling roles. Do not become the unpaid emotional support for the whole office. For money, she can be generous to a fault, so check your lending and favours. Put your own wellbeing on the budget before you pay for everyone else's.
yesNoText: Yes, if your heart agrees. The Queen of Cups favours emotional honesty, compassion and intuition, so it leans positive when the choice feels right in your gut. Reversed, the answer turns to maybe or no: confusion, over-giving or drained feelings are clouding your judgment.
melissaLine: You are not too sensitive, you are just reading the room accurately in a world that prefers you did not.

name: King of Cups
metaDescription: King of Cups tarot card meaning: upright, reversed, love and yes or no. Emotional balance, calm judgement and steady kindness.
intro: The King of Cups sits on a stone throne that floats on a rough sea, with a fish leaping on one side and a ship rocking behind. In one hand he holds a cup, in the other a sceptre, and he wears a fish pendant. The water is wild around him. He is calm. He is what emotional steadiness looks like.
upright:
He feels everything and does not let it run the meeting. The King of Cups is emotional maturity: compassion with boundaries, advice that is kind and practical, and the ability to stay level when other people are thrashing. The throne floats on the sea, which means he lives among emotions without being swallowed by them.

This card asks you to respond rather than react. Take the fifteen minutes before replying to the infuriating email. Let yourself be moved, then act deliberately. It also describes a person you can lean on: a mentor, a counsellor, a partner who stays calm in an argument. Be careful to check that calm is not a cover for suppression. Real balance includes saying what hurts, plainly, and then listening to the answer.
reversed:
Reversed, the King loses his footing. He may be emotionally manipulative, moody or cold, using charm to get his own way and silence to punish. It might also describe you bottling feelings until they erupt, or numbing them with work, wine or scrolling.

If someone is blowing hot and cold, notice that the pattern is the message. If it is you, find an outlet that is not a late-night rant: a long walk, a voice note to nobody, a conversation with someone safe. Stability is built, not announced, and it shows in how you behave when nobody is watching.
love: Single, look for emotional steadiness over fireworks: someone who communicates, apologises and does not go cold when things get awkward. You may also be the calm one, so do not tolerate chaos just to be useful. In a relationship, the King brings loyalty and kindness, with the caution not to hide behind composure. Talk about feelings before they leak out sideways. With an ex or situationship, beware charm with no accountability, and trust someone who is straightforward about what he wants.
career: Diplomacy and calm pay off. You may be the person colleagues bring problems to, or may need a mentor with that quality. Lead by listening, then decide. Counselling, mediation, teaching and healthcare are favoured. For money, steady and sensible choices win: set aside savings, avoid emotional spending and seek advice from a calm adviser. Keep personal drama out of negotiations, as composure is persuasive.
yesNoText: Yes, thoughtfully. The King of Cups favours wise, balanced decisions made with care for everyone involved, so it leans positive when you have thought it through. Reversed, the answer turns to no or maybe: moodiness, manipulation or suppressed feelings could undermine the outcome.
melissaLine: Feel it fully, then wait before you reply, because the calmest person in the room usually gets the best outcome.
